Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for the second numbered section use numbered list two one leave the current notification sound in place two turn on the desktop notice when a transfer pauses or fails three don't send email because the shared account is not monitored outside office hours four keep the warning visible until someone dismisses it but don't block access to other open windows mara may be comparing the checklist while a notice is present if there is a choice between warning about a paused transfer and hiding the notice after a short delay keep the warning visible

the last condition matters because the network test happens before the team begins moving the folders if the test share is reachable, leave the destination as cedar-box slash collections slash incoming and proceed with the dry run using only the folder named sample batch if the test share is not reachable, don't switch to the backup share and don't start the dry run just show the connection warning and leave the existing settings in place the backup share is read-only and is only used by the administrator later so don't treat it as an alternative destination

after the dry run, show the result on screen and leave the uploader open for mara to inspect it please don't claim that the weekly transfer is ready just because the sample batch worked she still has to compare the destination with her checklist and dev may notice a missing folder in the log if either of them finds a problem they will ask me before changing the profile one more thing the shared workstation is booked for a scanner test at 11:30 on thursday so finish the setup before then and don't schedule an automatic transfer that could start during the scanner test the team will start the actual transfer manually after the morning check

The machine is called juniper, and it runs the uploader from the tools folder, not from the shortcut on the desktop, because that shortcut still points to the old test profile. Please keep the existing profile name archive-main and do not make a second profile just to test the settings. The uploader is used by three people, but Mara is the person who checks the incoming files, so her name should stay in the notification list.

We are moving scans from the local intake folder to the storage share called cedar-box. The source folder is intake scans, and the destination is cedar-box slash collections slash incoming. There are 18 folders waiting now, and the team expects around 6 more before the end of the week. Those are estimates, not limits, so please don't set a maximum queue size from those numbers. The network is sometimes slow between 4 and 5 in the afternoon, and people may leave the workstation during a transfer, so a paused transfer needs to be able to continue rather than start over if the connection drops.

There is one setting I need you to find by its exact name and set to true. Please put the key by itself on a line:
transfer.allow_resume
Then set that key to true in the uploader preferences. Don't rename it or change the spelling. The support note says, “Resume is safe after a brief connection loss, but check the destination before retrying.” That is why Mara checks the destination before she asks anyone to retry a failed folder. I want that check to stay part of the routine.

For the first numbered section:
1. Confirm the source is intake scans and the destination is cedar-box slash collections slash incoming.
2. Confirm the active profile is archive-main and the notification still goes to Mara.
3. Leave automatic retry off because the team wants to review a failed folder before trying again.
4. Set the retry wait to 90 seconds, not 60. I said 60 at first, but the current team note says 90 seconds. Use the current note, and don't change the number of retries, which is 2.

The next part is about the copy behavior. The files are mostly TIFF scans and a few PDF forms, and the uploader should keep the original filenames, including spaces and parentheses. One folder has a file called intake sheet (signed).pdf, and another has a scan called 0048 west window.tif. Please don't normalize those names or replace spaces with underscores. The archive team compares the uploaded names against a paper checklist, so a rename could make the match harder. If a duplicate filename appears, the uploader should stop and show the conflict instead of replacing the file or silently adding a suffix.

Please set the completed-file action to leave a local copy in intake scans until Mara has checked the destination. She usually checks the first folder herself and then asks Dev to look at the remaining folders. If the destination is unavailable, the uploader should keep the local files and show a clear warning. The team does not want the program to delete a source file just because a transfer looked complete on the workstation. The confirmation should mention the folder name and the count of files, but it should not imply that Mara has approved the contents.

We also need a useful log, but not one that fills the shared drive. The log should stay in the uploader logs folder on juniper and keep entries for 14 days. The machine has 32 gigabytes of memory and 480 gigabytes free on the local disk. Those details are for checking that the setup is sensible, not instructions to reserve that much space. Please use the normal log size limit and include timestamps, file names, and transfer status. Do not record the contents of the files. The weekly review is on Friday morning, and Dev reads the log then, so use the local time shown on juniper and don't change its clock or time zone.

For the second numbered section:
1. Leave the current notification sound in place.
2. Turn on the desktop notice when a transfer pauses or fails.
3. Don't send email because the shared account is not monitored outside office hours.
4. Keep the warning visible until someone dismisses it, but don't block access to other open windows. Mara may be comparing the checklist while a notice is present. If there is a choice between warning about a paused transfer and hiding the notice after a short delay, keep the warning visible.

The last condition matters because the network test happens before the team begins moving the folders. If the test share is reachable, leave the destination as cedar-box slash collections slash incoming and proceed with the dry run using only the folder named sample batch. If the test share is not reachable, don't switch to the backup share and don't start the dry run; just show the connection warning and leave the existing settings in place. The backup share is read-only and is only used by the administrator later, so don't treat it as an alternative destination.

After the dry run, show the result on screen and leave the uploader open for Mara to inspect it. Please don't claim that the weekly transfer is ready just because the sample batch worked. She still has to compare the destination with her checklist, and Dev may notice a missing folder in the log. If either of them finds a problem, they will ask me before changing the profile. One more thing: the shared workstation is booked for a scanner test at 11:30 on Thursday, so finish the setup before then and don't schedule an automatic transfer that could start during the scanner test. The team will start the actual transfer manually after the morning check.

When you save the preferences, keep the profile archive-main selected and leave the source and destination fields visible at the end. If there is a confirmation box for applying the preferences, choose save only if the displayed profile is archive-main. If some other profile is displayed, stop at that box and tell me which profile is shown rather than saving over it. The team has had two profiles with similar names in the past, and the old test profile must remain untouched. After you finish, leave the log folder and the transfer summary available on screen so Mara can begin her check when she gets to juniper."}]
